summary: Frontend-only verification of the interest-rate HTML5 validation popup bug fix across 8 finance calculators via Playwright on the public URL. Verified (a) no HTML5 constraint validation error is possible on any numeric input (checkValidity()==true, validationMessage empty, step='any', no min/max attributes present on any input), and (b) compute() uses the EXACT decimal entered by cross-checking every result against independently computed EMI/FV/maturity values (node script). 11/11 requested scenarios PASS plus reset regression PASS. Also tested real keyboard typing (not just fill) and edge cases.

validation_gaps.issue: Removing min/max removed all bounds: entering rate -5 on home-loan-emi-calculator computes and displays 'Monthly EMI ₹12,084.53' with negative Total Interest (-₹20,99,711.85) and negative interest rows in the amortization table. Rate 0 yields ₹20,833.33 (mathematically OK). Recommend JS-level (not HTML5-attribute) validation showing a friendly inline message for out-of-range values, keeping step='any' so decimals like 8.5/8.46/5.875 stay valid.

verified_cases: home-loan-emi 8.46% -> ₹43,264.66 (independently computed 43,264.66; request note said ~43,262.61 which is slightly off — formula output is correct) PASS, distinct from 8.5% value
Reset restores rate=8.5, amount=5000000 and clears calc-results PASS
Typed (keystroke) 8.5 -> checkValidity()=true, validationMessage='' , calculate succeeds PASS
Empty rate -> calculate-btn correctly disabled PASS
No browser dialog/validation tooltip fired on any page (dialog listener attached, zero events); no console errors
action_items: Optional: add JS-based range validation with inline error for negative/absurd rate & amount values (keep step='any', do NOT reintroduce HTML5 min/max/step-numeric which caused the original popup bug).
critical_code_review_comments: finance.js input definitions still carry unused min/max/step keys that CalculatorRenderer ignores — dead metadata; either use them for soft JS validation or remove to avoid confusion.
buildAmortization loops per-month in render path; fine for 40y but consider memoizing if breakdown grows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix (step='any', no min/max) is fully verified across all 8 finance calculators; math matches independent computation exactly. Only remaining observation is the absence of any range validation (negative rate accepted). Use data-testids input-{key} where key comes from finance.js (e.g. input-curRate, input-newRate, input-principal, input-monthly).
rca_of_the_issue: Original popup came from HTML5 stepMismatch: step=0.05 with min=0.01 made 8.5 an invalid step value, so the browser blocked submit with a 'nearest valid value' tooltip. Fix removes min/max and sets step='any', eliminating stepMismatch/rangeUnderflow entirely — confirmed via input.checkValidity() returning true and empty validationMessage on every field.
